content.title: LA 2028 Olympic ticket prices come with ‘insane’ hidden charges leaving fans outraged at staggering costs
content.text: FANS have been left outraged by large service fees driving the cost of LA 2028 tickets even higher. Tickets for the event went on presale last week, but users logging on to snag themselves a spot at the event were struck with a hefty surcharge. Sign up for the Sport newsletter Thank you! Fans purchasing tickets for the 2028 LA Olympics have been confused by a hefty service feeCredit: LA 28 Prices were already nothing to scoff at, with some costs for the opening ceremony reaching well into the thousands. But a portion of the listed prices are actually made up of a hidden service charge. Users reported that the service charge was calculated not as a flat fee, but as a percentage of the ticket price itself. And it is not a small chunk of the cost, with the fee coming to 24 per cent of the tickets’ costs. One fan said on X: “I think top tier tickets for the Opening Ceremony were over $5,000. Lower middle tier pricing was about $1,300. “BUT they add a super high “service fee” – opening ceremony service fee for our tickets was $312.39 per ticket!!!” Another user shared a screenshot showing a $1,890 price tag for two tickets to the men’s soccer final, with the service charge alone making up $365 of that fee. Fans are not clear what the service fee is actually contributing to, especially given that it is calculated as a percentage of the ticket price, and seemingly not based on any specific services being carried out. Most read in Sport One Manhattan Beach resident – who claims she was given a service fee of $505 for a $2,100 ticket at the Games- told the LAist: “It’s insane, I don’t understand what the service is.” The prices and fees have already been enough to turn some people off from attempting to secure seats at the Games, despite general sale not opening until Thursday. Almost a quarter of a ticket’s price goes towards a service chargeCredit: AFP One fan said: “The service fee on the LA Olympics tickets looking like I’m better off buying an orange vest and a ladder.” Another added: “Damn, that tv broadcast is looking really good now.” One fan even compared the listed prices to what they spent at the previous Games in Paris, noting a 4x increase in total costs for the same event. They wrote: “Comparing pricing of the LA tickets vs what I paid for Paris is shocking. Approx. 400% increase / 4x jump in cost. “Additionally the service fee for LA is 25% vs Paris 1.5%. I assumed LA would be more expensive….but 400% more?” They listed the price they claim to have paid for a Group B Athletics ticket at both games. “Paris Athletics (Group B) $550 ticket + $16 service fee. “LA Athletics (Group B) $2,050 ticket (including $510 service fee).” The controversy arrives at the same time that ticket prices for the upcoming World Cup are causing fans distress. A ticket to the final will set fans back in the region of $11,000, and has been touted as the most expensive soccer ticket ever. And it is not just the tickets themselves burning a hole in fans’ pockets. The Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority (MBTA) has hiked up the price of a return fare to World Cup venue Foxborough Stadium, from $20 to $80. Comments
